rest.notary.answers.missingToken: Any endpoint, when the request reaches notary without an `Authorization` header holding a `Bearer` token. Notary checks the token itself, after Kong. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer`.
rest.notary.answers.tokenRefused: Any endpoint, when the token passes Kong but fails notary's own check: signed by a key identity does not publish, another issuer or audience, an algorithm other than RS256, an issue time in the future, or an expiry passed by more than 30 seconds. Refresh the token, or sign in again.
rest.notary.answers.notAccessToken: Any endpoint, when the token is a valid identity token but not an access token, such as a refresh token or a two-factor challenge token. Send the access token.
rest.notary.answers.unknownPath: Any path under `/api/v1/proofs` that notary does not serve, whatever the method: `/api/v1/proofs` itself, a path with a trailing slash, an evidence path without its order number or review id.
rest.notary.answers.methodNotAllowed: Any path notary serves, when the request uses a method that path does not answer. `Allow` lists the methods it does: `GET, HEAD` for proofs and evidence, `GET, HEAD, POST` for registrations. Through Kong only an `OPTIONS` request that Kong passes on can arrive this way.
rest.notary.answers.identityUnavailable: Any endpoint, when the token names a signing key notary has not read yet and identity's published keys cannot be fetched. The token was not judged; retry later.
rest.notary.answers.database: `GET /api/v1/proofs/liabilities/{epoch}`, `POST /api/v1/proofs/registrations` and both evidence endpoints, when notary cannot read or write its database. Nothing can be said about the answer; retry later. A retried registration is not stored twice.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.summary: Answers the caller's inclusion proofs for one epoch, a commitment to everything Kinetix owed its account holders at one moment: one proof per account the caller holds, with the account opened and a statement signed for the court. Each entry of `proofs` is a self-contained document a verifier checks against the ledger on chain.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.who: Any signed-in principal. The proofs are only ever the caller's own accounts, matched on the token's principal: customer balance, merchant available and pending escrow, courier available and pending escrow.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.field.epoch: A decimal epoch number, digits only and without a leading zero, at most 2⁶³ − 1; or `latest` for the newest final epoch.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.proven: The epoch is final and the caller holds accounts in it: one document per account, in the order of the tree. Keep each document whole, since a verifier checks every field. `format` is `kinetix.notary.inclusion.v2` when the document carries the account's `secret`, `kinetix.notary.inclusion.v1` otherwise; `scheme` `2` is a confidential epoch, whose sibling sums are `0`. `epoch`, `amount`, `index` and the sums are decimal strings, and amounts are in minor units.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.noAccou: The epoch is final and the caller holds no account in it, so `proofs` is empty. Kinetix owed this principal nothing at that epoch.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.invalid: `epoch` breaks its rule; `message` says how. It is not `latest` and not written in digits only, as here; or it is a number above 2⁶³ − 1, the highest epoch number, and `message` says it `is above` that limit; or it has a leading zero, such as `007`, and `message` says it `is written with a leading zero`. Fix the path; asking again unchanged gets the same answer.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.noneFin: `latest` was asked and no epoch is final yet.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.neverBu: No epoch with this number was ever built. Ask for `latest`, or for a number no higher than its `epoch`.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.notFina: The epoch is built but not final yet; `message` names its state: `built`, `submitted` or `mined`. Ask again later.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.abandon: The epoch was abandoned and never anchored, so no proof for it will ever exist. Ask for another epoch.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.failed: Notary found its own records inconsistent (`error` is `disagreement`) or failed in another way of its own (`internal`). `message` never says more. Nothing was changed; a retry is safe but may fail the same way.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.signerU: The court names no signer for the epoch, notary holds no key for the one it names, or signing failed, so no statement can be signed. Retry later.
rest.notary.liabilityProofs.case.chainUn: Notary could not read the epoch's signer from the chain. Retry later.
rest.notary.registrationTemplate.summary: Answers the EIP-712 typed data a holder signs to register a wallet address with the withholding court: the types, the court's domain and the caller's `principal`. Add `holder` and `issuedAt` to `message` and sign the rest unchanged, with `eth_signTypedData_v4`.
rest.notary.registrationTemplate.who: Any signed-in principal; `message.principal` is the token's principal.
rest.notary.registrationTemplate.case.te: Always, once the token is accepted. `domain.chainId` is a JSON number here, unlike the decimal strings elsewhere in notary's answers. Set `message.holder` to the address that signs and `message.issuedAt` to the current Unix time in seconds, then post the signature to `POST /api/v1/proofs/registrations` within 5 minutes.
rest.notary.register.summary: Registers the wallet address `holder` for every account the caller holds in the latest final epoch, and answers the registrations notary signed for them. With a registration, that address can ask the withholding court on chain for a statement of its account from `fromEpoch` on.
rest.notary.register.who: Any signed-in principal with an account in the latest final epoch. The signature must come from `holder` and cover the token's principal, so an address is registered only by whoever holds its key, and only for the caller's own accounts.
rest.notary.register.field.holder: The address to register: `0x` and 40 hexadecimal digits, not the zero address. The signature must recover to it.
rest.notary.register.field.issuedAt: The `issuedAt` that was signed: Unix seconds as a decimal string, above 0. Accepted from 5 minutes before to 1 minute after notary's clock.
rest.notary.register.field.signature: The EIP-712 signature by `holder` over the template of `GET /api/v1/proofs/registrations` with `holder` and `issuedAt` filled in: `0x` and 130 hexadecimal digits, `r`, `s` and `v`. `s` must be in the lower half of the curve order, and `v` 0, 1, 27 or 28.
rest.notary.register.case.registered: One registration per account the caller holds in `epoch`, the latest final epoch, which is also each one's `fromEpoch`; `court` is the withholding court they are for. Keep every registration whole: the holder presents its `digest` and `signature` on chain. Posting again is safe; a later final epoch gives registrations from that epoch.
rest.notary.register.case.malformed: The body is not one JSON object with `holder`, `issuedAt` and `signature` as strings and no other field, or it is larger than 4 KiB. A number for `issuedAt` is refused here too.
rest.notary.register.case.trailing: Something follows the JSON object in the body.
rest.notary.register.case.invalidField: A field breaks its rule. `message` is one of `holder is not an address`, `holder is the zero address`, `issuedAt is not a decimal number of seconds`, `issuedAt is not a time` or `signature is not 65 bytes of hex`; the fields are checked in that order and only the first failure is reported.
rest.notary.register.case.stale: `issuedAt` is more than 5 minutes before notary's clock: the request was signed too long ago. Sign a new request with the current time.
rest.notary.register.case.issuedAhead: `issuedAt` is more than 1 minute after notary's clock, usually because the device's clock runs ahead. Correct the clock, or sign again with an `issuedAt` no later than now.
rest.notary.register.case.wrongSigner: The signature recovers to an address other than `holder`: another key made it, or it covers other values, such as another principal, another `issuedAt` or another domain. Sign the served template again with the key of `holder`.
rest.notary.register.case.badSignature: The signature is not a canonical secp256k1 signature (`v` not 0, 1, 27 or 28, `r` or `s` out of range, or `s` in the upper half), or no key recovers from it, which `message` gives as `the signature recovers no key`.
rest.notary.register.case.noAccount: The latest final epoch holds no account of the caller, so there is nothing to register. Try again after a final epoch that includes one.
rest.notary.register.case.noneFinal: No epoch is final yet. Try again after the first one is.
rest.notary.register.case.beforeSecrets: The latest final epoch was built before accounts carried secrets, so registration opens with the next final epoch. Try again then.
rest.notary.register.case.failed: Notary found its own records inconsistent (`error` is `disagreement`) or failed in another way of its own (`internal`). `message` never says more. No registration was saved.
rest.notary.register.case.signerUnavaila: The court names no signer for the epoch, notary holds no key for the one it names, or signing failed. Nothing was saved; retry later.
rest.notary.register.case.chainUnavailab: Notary could not read the epoch's signer from the chain. Nothing was saved; retry later.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.summary: Answers inclusion proofs for the records notary keeps about one order: its lifecycle changes, read from order, and its delivery, read from matching. Each proof shows that its record was committed in a batch anchored on chain, without revealing any other record.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.who: Any signed-in principal, for the records it is a party to: a lifecycle record to the order's buyer and merchant and to whoever acted, a delivery record to the courier who delivered and to the order's buyer and merchant.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.field.order: The order number, for example `ORD-20261021-3F9A1C7B`. Once percent-decoded: at most 255 bytes, valid UTF-8, no NUL byte.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.case.proven: The caller is a party to records of the order and at least one is in a final batch. `proofs` holds one document per such record, carrying either `lifecycle` or `delivery`, its `salt`, its leaf `index` and the `siblings` up to the batch's `root`. `pending` counts the caller's records not yet in a final batch; ask again later for those. The codes in `lifecycle` are those of the order lifecycle contract, record times are RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, and `closedAt` is Unix seconds.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.case.pending: The caller is a party to records of the order, but none is in a final batch yet: `proofs` is empty and `pending` counts them. Ask again later.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.case.invalidRe: The order number, once percent-decoded, is longer than 255 bytes (as here, with its length), is not valid UTF-8 (`message`: `the order reference is not valid UTF-8`), or carries a NUL byte such as `%00` (`message`: `the order reference carries a NUL byte`). No order number has any of these; fix the path.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.case.noEvidenc: Notary keeps no record of this order that the caller is a party to. An unknown order and someone else's order are answered the same way.
rest.notary.orderEvidence.case.failed: Notary's records of the order disagree with what it anchored (`error` is `disagreement`), or it failed in another way of its own (`internal`). `message` never says more. A retry is safe but may fail the same way.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.summary: Answers the inclusion proof for the record notary keeps of one review, a product review or a courier rating, read from review. The proof shows that the record was committed in a batch anchored on chain.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.who: Any signed-in principal party to the review: its author, plus the merchant for a product review or the rated courier for a courier rating.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.field.review: The review's id, the UUID review answers as `id` on `201` or as `review_id` on `409`. Once percent-decoded: at most 255 bytes, valid UTF-8, no NUL byte.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.case.proven: The review's record is in a final batch, so `proofs` holds its document and `pending` is `0`. In `review`, `kind` is `1` for a product review, whose `subjectId` is the product, and `2` for a courier rating, whose `subjectId` is the courier's principal. `commentSha256` is the SHA-256 of the comment and is left out when the review has none.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.case.pending: The review's record is not in a final batch yet: `proofs` is empty and `pending` is `1`. Ask again later.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.case.invalidR: The review id, once percent-decoded, is not valid UTF-8 (as here), is longer than 255 bytes (`message` gives its length: `the review reference is 300 bytes, more than 255`), or carries a NUL byte such as `%00` (`message`: `the review reference carries a NUL byte`). No review id has any of these; fix the path.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.case.noEviden: Notary keeps no record of this review that the caller is a party to. An unknown review and someone else's review are answered the same way.
rest.notary.reviewEvidence.case.failed: Notary's record of the review disagrees with what it anchored (`error` is `disagreement`), or it failed in another way of its own (`internal`). `message` never says more. A retry is safe but may fail the same way.
